groups.title: Tablet (A06600ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation, loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 1 tablet per dose, 3 times in 1 day, before meals (between meals or after meals). Ages 11 years to under 15 years: take 1 tablet per dose, 2 times in 1 day, before meals (between meals or after meals). Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses; for the first dose take the smallest amount and then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not give this medicine to anyone with an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like), to anyone with intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel), or to a child aged 7 years or younger.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if you have kidney impairment; or if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure.

If symptoms do not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian.

Do not take this medicine within 1 hour after an antacid or after drinking milk.

If rash (reddening of the skin), itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Enteric-coated Tablet (292800ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of constipation and of the loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that follow constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 3 tablets per dose. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: take 2 tablets per dose. Take it 1 time in 1 day at bedtime (on an empty stomach). For the first dose take the smallest amount, then increase or decrease it gradually while watching the form and condition of the stool.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger; if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like) or intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel); or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a child aged 10 years or younger; if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure; if you are on a sodium-restricted diet; or if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or Yellow No. 5.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Do not chew the tablet when taking it. If constipation does not improve after about 1 week of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an antacid. Avoid taking it within 1 hour after drinking milk.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Soft Capsule (D22200ACS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age; or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if the user is a baby or young child aged 3 months or older and under 2 years of age; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver, kidney, heart or thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. Do not drink alcohol while taking it. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like), an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you have been given barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor, insomnia, signs of shock (rarely urticaria, swelling and chest tightness after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (high fever with rash and reddening and severe burn-like blisters), acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, a severe skin adverse reaction such as fever, erythema and many small pustules, asthma, general lassitude, jaundice, interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever), or symptoms of ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 tablets per dose, 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.

groups.title: Enteric-coated Tablet (111001ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to inhibit the formation of blood clots in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction and unstable angina, to inhibit the formation of blood clots after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG) or percutaneous transluminal coronary angioplasty (PTCA), and to reduce cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients (people with combined risk factors such as a family history of ischaemic heart disease, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol, obesity or diabetes).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 tablet per dose, 1 time in 1 day. As this is an enteric-coated tablet, it may be taken before meals with plenty of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to another salicylate preparation; if you have peptic ulcer; if you have or have had aspirin asthma; if you have haemophilia, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or a tendency to bleed; if you are being given methotrexate at a dose of 15 milligrams or more a week (15 mg a week); or if you are in the third trimester of pregnancy.

In the first and second trimesters of pregnancy, do not take this medicine unless it is really necessary.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have kidney impairment; if you have impaired cardiovascular circulation (renal vascular disease, congestive heart failure, reduced body fluid, major surgery, sepsis or a major bleeding event and the like); if you have or have had liver impairment; if you have impaired heart function; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are about to have surgery; if the user is a young child aged 3 years or younger; if you have hypersensitivity to analgesics, anti-inflammatory medicines or antirheumatic medicines, or an allergic disease; if you are an older person; if you have glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency; if you have Reye's syndrome; if the user is aged 14 years or younger with chickenpox or influenza infection; or if you have gout.

Because there is a risk of bleeding, tell your doctor that you are taking this medicine if you are to have surgery (including dental surgery). Take care not to damage the enteric coating of this medicine.

Do not use it together with a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or high-dose methotrexate (15 mg a week or more), because bleeding may increase or kidney function may decline when they are given with this medicine.

Consult a pharmacist if you are taking an anticoagulant, a thrombolytic, another platelet aggregation inhibitor, a haemostatic, a diabetes medicine (insulin preparations, tolbutamide and the like), a uricosuric (benzbromarone, probenecid), low-dose methotrexate, a lithium preparation, some non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesics such as ibuprofen or naproxen, a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor, digoxin, a systemic corticosteroid (except hydrocortisone used as replacement therapy for Addison's disease), an angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor or a valproic acid preparation. Do not mix it with an alkaline preparation (for example sodium bicarbonate or magnesium carbonate) or with a preparation that easily takes up moisture. When it is taken with alcohol, damage to the gastrointestinal mucosa increases and bleeding time may be prolonged through the combined effect of this medicine and alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: shock and anaphylactic symptoms (difficulty breathing, generalised flushing, angioedema, urticaria); an asthma attack; hypersensitivity (erythema, itching, blocked nose, cardiac and respiratory disturbance, occasionally rash, swelling, urticaria, rhinitis-like symptoms, conjunctivitis); rarely toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); drug reaction with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome) with fever, rash, lymphadenopathy, facial swelling, hepatitis, nephritis, blood abnormalities, myocarditis or myositis; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome); exfoliative dermatitis; aplastic anaemia, anaemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time); haemolysis and haemolytic anaemia in people with severe glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency; loss of appetite, heartburn, stomach pain, nausea, vomiting; ringing in the ears, hearing loss, dizziness, headache, excitement; rarely liver impairment; very rarely temporary liver damage, kidney impairment, acute renal failure, hyperventilation or metabolic acidosis; Conn's syndrome of unknown frequency (cardiovascular symptoms occurring after an allergy or hypersensitivity reaction associated with coronary artery constriction); an excessive fall in body temperature, collapse or cold limbs.

summaryTable.What it is for: Inhibiting blood clot formation in myocardial infarction, cerebral infarction and unstable angina, after CABG or PTCA, and reducing cardiovascular risk in high-risk patients

groups.title: Tablet (D07901ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used as an aid in the treatment of osteoporosis, for the prevention of the risk of vitamin D deficiency disease in healthy people without malabsorption, and for the prevention of rickets.
groups.usage: As an aid in the treatment of osteoporosis, adults: take 1 tablet (1000 IU) per dose, 1 time in 1 day. For healthy people without malabsorption and for the prevention of rickets, adults: take 1/2 tablet (500 IU) per dose, 1 time in 1 day. For a young child who has difficulty swallowing the tablet, place the tablet on a spoon, let it disintegrate in water and, if possible, take it with a meal. Take it with plenty of water.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have high blood calcium or high calcium in the urine; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; if you have kidney stones; or if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 1 year of age; if the user is a child who gets plenty of sunlight and eats a normal diet; if you have a history of kidney stones; if you have sarcoidosis; if your movement is restricted (a plaster cast); if you have pseudohypoparathyroidism; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; or if you have kidney impairment.

A young child who has difficulty swallowing this medicine should take the tablet after it has been dissolved in water.

Do not take it together with a benzothiadiazine derivative. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with another vitamin D preparation, phenytoin or a barbiturate medicine, a thiazide diuretic or a glucocorticoid.

If mental symptoms or disturbance of consciousness (raised blood calcium), headache, nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, weight loss or increased thirst (raised blood calcium), acute symptoms of raised blood calcium (arrhythmia, nausea, vomiting, mental symptoms, disturbance of consciousness), chronic symptoms of raised blood calcium (increased urge to pass urine, increased thirst, loss of appetite, weight loss, kidney stones, calcification of the kidney, calcification in the tissue outside the bone), or muscle and joint pain occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Powder (113232APD)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for acute and chronic enteritis, acute and chronic diarrhoea, acute dysentery, and abnormal fermentation in the intestine due to various causes.
groups.usage: Adults: take 2 g per dose, 3 times in 1 day; for the first dose take 4 g. Infants and young children: take 1 g per dose, 3 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby under 3 months of age.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. If symptoms do not improve after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Consult a pharmacist if you use it together with ciprofloxacin, imipenem or cilastatin sodium.

groups.title: Tablet (383800ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for headache, toothache, joint pain, neuralgia, muscle pain, pain from a sprain and menstrual pain (period pain).
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day, avoiding an empty stomach. Leave an interval of at least 4 hours between doses.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Do not take this medicine if you have or have had hypersensitivity to it (for example rash, reddening of the skin, itching, swelling of the throat, eyelids or lips); if you have had an asthma attack after taking another antipyretic analgesic (non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic) or a cold medicine; if you have peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment or severely reduced heart function; or if you have taken barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have a constitution prone to allergy or have had allergic symptoms (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have thyroid disease, diabetes or high blood pressure; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have had peptic ulcer; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have impaired heart function; if you have a history of hypersensitivity reactions; if you have bronchial asthma; if you are an older person; or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Do not take it together with other products containing acetaminophen, another antipyretic analgesic, another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, a cold medicine, a sedative, barbiturates or tricyclic antidepressants. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with warfarin, lithium, a thiazide diuretic or levodopa.

If signs of shock (difficulty breathing, flushing of the whole body, angioedema, urticaria, an asthma attack, swelling of the throat, eyelids or lips, chest tightness, pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat, breathlessness), thrombocytopenia, granulocytopenia, haemolytic anaemia, methaemoglobinaemia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time), cyanosis, a hypersensitivity reaction (facial swelling, low blood pressure), nausea, vomiting, loss of appetite, gastrointestinal bleeding, peptic ulcer, perforation, rash, Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (severe symptoms with high fever, rash, reddening of the skin and burn-like blisters on the skin of the whole body and on the mouth and eye membranes), general lassitude, jaundice, cough with breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever, high anion gap metabolic acidosis (HAGMA), an excessive fall in body temperature, collapse or cold limbs occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Tablet (199501ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis (degenerative joint disease), ankylosing spondylitis, tendinitis, acute gout, dysmenorrhoea, bursitis, skeletal muscle disorders (sprain, contusion, injury, lumbosacral pain), pain after surgery, migraine and pain after tooth extraction.
groups.usage: For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis and ankylosing spondylitis, adults: take 1 to 2 tablets (275 to 550 mg) per dose, 2 times in 1 day (every 12 hours). For acute gout: take 3 tablets (825 mg) as the first dose, then 1 tablet (275 mg) at intervals of 8 hours until the attack settles. For skeletal muscle disorders, pain after surgery, pain after tooth extraction, dysmenorrhoea, tendinitis and bursitis: take 2 tablets (550 mg) as the first dose, then 1 tablet (275 mg) at intervals of 6 to 8 hours, without exceeding a total of 5 tablets (1375 mg) in 1 day. For migraine: take 3 tablets (825 mg) as the first dose; if needed, 1 to 2 further tablets (275 to 550 mg) may be taken in 1 day, 30 minutes after the first dose. Do not exceed a total of 5 tablets (1375 mg) in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency, severe kidney impairment or severe high blood pressure; if you have hypersensitivity to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic; if you have or have had asthma, rhinitis, nasal polyps, urticaria or an allergic reaction caused by aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); if it is for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery; if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption; if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; or if the user is a baby aged 2 years or younger.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a child; if you are an older person; if you have had peptic ulcer or a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have impaired heart function, high blood pressure or bronchial asthma; or if you have systemic lupus erythematosus or mixed connective tissue disease.

Do not take it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic or naproxen derivative, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a hydantoin antiepileptic, a sulfonamide, a sulfonylurea blood-glucose-lowering medicine, propranolol or another beta blocker, an ACE inhibitor (captopril and the like), a loop or thiazide diuretic, probenecid, lithium, low-dose methotrexate, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like), zidovudine or a new quinolone antibiotic (enoxacin and the like).

groups.title: Enteric-coated Tablet (292800ATE)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for constipation and for the relief of loss of appetite, abdominal distension, abnormal fermentation in the intestine and haemorrhoids that accompany constipation.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 tablets per dose. Ages 11 years to under 15 years: take 1 to 2 tablets per dose. Ages 7 years to under 11 years: take 1 tablet per dose. groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if the user is a child aged 7 years or younger; if you have an acute abdominal disease (appendicitis, intestinal bleeding, ulcerative colitis and the like) or intestinal obstruction (blocked bowel); or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or may be pregnant; if the user is a child aged 10 years or younger; if you have severe abdominal pain, nausea or vomiting; if you have kidney impairment; if you have had rectal bleeding or intestinal failure; if you have or have had hypersensitivity to Yellow No. 4 or Yellow No. 5; or if you are on a sodium-restricted diet.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, severe abdominal pain, diarrhoea, vomiting, abdominal discomfort or cramps occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

groups.title: Syrup (142334ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to reduce fever caused by an acute upper respiratory tract infection.
groups.usage: Children aged 6 months and older: take 0.4 to 0.6 mL per kg of body weight (5 to 7 mg per kg) per dose at intervals of 4 to 6 hours when needed, without exceeding 4 doses (28 mg per kg) in 1 day. For a child weighing 30 kg or less, do not exceed 25 mL (300 mg) in 1 day. If the body weight is known, dosing by body weight is more appropriate; refer to the approved product information for the recommended dose for each age group.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, peptic ulcer, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction to aspirin or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic (including COX-2 inhibitors); if it is for the treatment of pain occurring before or after coronary artery bypass graft surgery (CABG); or if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have had peptic ulcer; if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed (platelet dysfunction may occur); if you have or have had liver impairment or kidney impairment; if you have cardiac insufficiency or high blood pressure; if you have a history of hypersensitivity; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD); if you have ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if you are an older person or the user is a child; or if you have stomach cancer.

Considering the importance of the treatment, either stop breast-feeding or stop taking the medicine. Dizziness or fatigue may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. When it is taken for a long period for an acute illness, as a rule this should be within 5 days.

Do not take it together with another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic, aspirin or high-dose methotrexate. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a glucocorticoid, alcohol, digoxin, phenytoin, probenecid, sulfinpyrazone, a sulfonylurea, a diuretic, an antihypertensive, an ACE inhibitor, furosemide, lithium, low-dose methotrexate, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like) or low-dose aspirin.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: rarely shock (difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); blood disorders such as aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome) and toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome); triggering of an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura; occasionally rash or itching; rarely loss of vision or visual disturbance such as scotoma; aseptic meningitis; acute renal failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, or high blood potassium.

Occasionally loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea or stomach discomfort; very rarely thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension or constipation; rarely jaundice, raised GOT, GPT or AL-P, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude, or acute pulmonary oedema; occasionally swelling around the eye sockets; and very rarely malaise, fever or nosebleed may occur.

The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. In people with kidney impairment the dosing interval must be adjusted to kidney function, and in children with kidney impairment the dose must be adjusted individually according to renal clearance and body weight, so refer to the approved product information for details.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it or to hydroxyzine or piperazine derivatives; if you have renal failure; if the user is a young child under 6 years of age; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you are pregnant or breast-feeding; if you have kidney impairment or liver impairment; if you are an older person; if you have epilepsy or a risk of seizures; or if you have a predisposing factor for urinary retention (spinal cord lesion, prostatic hyperplasia and the like).

While you are taking this medicine, do not take it together with theophylline, ritonavir or a large amount of alcohol.

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: drowsiness, headache; occasionally lassitude, numbness, weakness, agitation or abnormal sensation; rarely mild and temporary listlessness, fatigue, dizziness, a heavy head, excitement, convulsions, movement disorder, dystonia, fainting, tremor, aggression, confusion, depression, hallucination, insomnia, tic disorder, loss of memory, memory disturbance, suicidal ideation or nightmares; occasionally thirst, dry lips, nausea, loss of appetite, stomach discomfort, indigestion, abdominal pain, stomach pain, abdominal discomfort or diarrhoea; rarely vomiting, gastrointestinal disturbance, inflammation of the lips, taste disturbance or increased appetite; rarely rapid heartbeat, arrhythmia or raised blood pressure; occasionally palpitations or vasculitis; occasionally reduced white blood cells, reduced neutrophils, increased lymphocytes or increased eosinophils; rarely increased monocytes, increased or reduced platelets, or photosensitivity; rarely hypersensitivity and anaphylactic shock; occasionally swelling, itching or rash; rarely urticaria, angioneurotic oedema, fixed drug eruption or acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; rarely blurred vision, conjunctival congestion, disturbance of eye accommodation, oculogyric crisis or vertigo; occasionally liver function disturbance such as raised AST, ALT, ALP, total bilirubin, gamma-GTP or LDH, jaundice, hepatitis, raised BUN, sugar in the urine or blood in the urine; rarely difficulty passing urine, bed-wetting or urinary retention; joint pain, muscle pain, pharyngitis, cough, nosebleed, bronchospasm, hearing disturbance or visual disturbance; occasionally chest pain; rarely menstrual disturbance, ringing in the ears, rhinitis or weight gain.

Itching, urticaria and the like may appear after this medicine is stopped.

groups.title: Syrup (172804ASY)

groups.usage: For rheumatoid arthritis, osteoarthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, soft tissue injury, non-articular rheumatic disease, acute gout and psoriatic arthritis, adults: take 200 to 600 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day; up to 3200 mg may be given in 1 day. For juvenile rheumatoid arthritis: take 30 to 40 mg per kg of body weight in 1 day, divided into 3 to 4 doses. For mild to moderate pain and for a cold, adults: take 200 to 400 mg per dose, 3 to 4 times in 1 day. The dose may be increased or decreased appropriately according to age and symptoms. A child weighing less than 30 kg must not be given more than 500 mg in 1 day, and it is better to avoid taking it on an empty stomach. Ages 11 to 14 years: take 200 to 250 mg (10 to 13 mL) per dose. Ages 7 to 10 years: take 150 to 200 mg (8 to 10 mL) per dose. Ages 3 to 6 years: take 100 to 150 mg (5 to 8 mL) per dose. Ages 1 to 2 years: take 50 to 100 mg (3 to 5 mL) per dose. Take it 3 to 4 times in 1 day.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause gastrointestinal bleeding.

Taking this medicine increases the risk of serious and possibly fatal cardiovascular thrombotic events, myocardial infarction and stroke, and serious gastrointestinal adverse reactions such as gastrointestinal bleeding, ulceration and perforation may occur.

People with uncontrolled high blood pressure, congestive heart failure, established ischaemic heart disease, peripheral arterial disease or cerebrovascular disease must avoid high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day); people with cardiovascular risk factors (high blood pressure, high blood lipids, diabetes, smoking and the like) who need high-dose ibuprofen (2,400 mg a day) must consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, a severe blood disorder, severe liver impairment, severe kidney impairment, severe cardiac insufficiency or severe high blood pressure; if you have or have had bronchial asthma; if you have had asthma, urticaria or an allergic reaction caused by aspirin or another anti-inflammatory analgesic; if pain occurs before or after coronary artery bypass surgery; if you are in the last 3 months of pregnancy; if you are breast-feeding; or if you are being given high-dose methotrexate as cancer treatment.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if you have or have had a blood disorder; if you have a tendency to bleed; if you have liver cirrhosis, or liver impairment now or in the past; if you have kidney impairment now or in the past; if you have cardiac insufficiency or heart disease or high blood pressure; if you have had hypersensitivity; if you have systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) or mixed connective tissue disease (MCTD); if you have ulcerative colitis or Crohn's disease; if you are an older person or the user is a child; or if you are pregnant or breast-feeding.

Without the instruction of a doctor or pharmacist, do not take it for pain for 10 days or more (adults) or 5 days or more (children), and do not take it for fever for 3 days or more.

Do not take it together with high-dose methotrexate or another non-steroidal anti-inflammatory analgesic. Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with low-dose aspirin, an ACE inhibitor, lithium, furosemide or a thiazide diuretic, methotrexate, a coumarin anticoagulant (warfarin and the like) or a selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI).

If any of the following occur, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist: shock (difficulty breathing, a fall in blood pressure and the like); blood disorders such as reduced haematocrit, reduced haemoglobin, anaemia, aplastic anaemia, haemolytic anaemia, agranulocytosis, granulocytopenia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, reduced platelet function (prolonged bleeding time) or eosinophilia; peptic ulcer, gastrointestinal ulcer, gastrointestinal bleeding, perforation, ulcerative colitis, bloody stools, gastritis, pancreatitis, vomiting of blood, Crohn's disease, loss of appetite, nausea, vomiting, abdominal pain, indigestion, diarrhoea, stomach discomfort, upper abdominal pain, thirst, stomatitis, abdominal distension, mouth ulcers, constipation, black stools; Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (Lyell's syndrome), photosensitivity reactions, drug rash with eosinophilia and systemic symptoms (DRESS syndrome), angioneurotic oedema, bullous dermatitis, erythema multiforme, maculopapular rash, reddening of the skin, blisters, rash, exfoliative dermatitis, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis; hepatitis, jaundice, abnormal liver function such as raised GOT, GPT or alkaline phosphatase (ALP), liver impairment; an asthma attack, urticaria, eczema, purpura, itching, asthma, bronchoconstriction or wheezing; visual disturbance such as scotoma, hearing loss, ringing in the ears, taste disturbance, vertigo, drowsiness, dizziness, depression, headache, a cerebrovascular event or nervousness; aseptic meningitis or meningitis (severe headache, nausea, vomiting, insomnia, a stiff neck, fever or disturbance of consciousness); a fall or rise in blood pressure, palpitations, heart failure, myocardial infarction or angina; acute renal failure, reduced urine output, blood in the urine, protein in the urine, raised BUN or blood creatinine, high blood potassium, interstitial nephritis, nephrotic syndrome, renal papillary necrosis, reduced urine volume, generalised oedema with breathlessness or lassitude; swelling around the eyes, swelling of the face, malaise, fever, nosebleed, oedema or peripheral oedema.

groups.title: Capsule (D94200ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of the various symptoms of a cold (runny nose, blocked nose, sneezing, sore throat, cough, phlegm, chills with shivering, fever, headache, joint pain, muscle pain).
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 15 years and older: take 2 capsules per dose. Ages 8 years to under 15 years: take 1 capsule per dose. Take it 3 times in 1 day, 30 minutes after meals.
groups.caution:
If you regularly drink three or more glasses of alcohol a day, consult a pharmacist before taking this medicine or any other antipyretic analgesic. It may cause liver damage.

Very rarely, serious skin reactions that may be fatal, such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis, Stevens-Johnson syndrome and toxic epidermal necrolysis, have been reported. If a skin rash or any other sign of hypersensitivity appears after taking this medicine, stop taking it immediately.

Do not exceed the maximum daily dose of acetaminophen (4,000 mg). It may cause liver damage. Do not take it together with other products that contain acetaminophen.

If a severe skin adverse reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it; if you have had asthma after taking another antipyretic analgesic or a cold medicine; if the user is a baby under 3 months of age or a child under 2 years of age; if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or have stopped taking one within the past 2 weeks; or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption.

Before taking this medicine, consult a pharmacist if the user is a baby or a child under 15 years of age with, or suspected of having, chickenpox or influenza; if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma or itching); if you have liver disease, kidney disease, heart disease, thyroid disease, diabetes, high blood pressure, gastric or duodenal ulcer, glaucoma (for example eye pain or blurred vision) or difficulty passing urine; if you are an older person, physically weak or have a high fever; if you have persistent or recurring stomach problems such as heartburn, stomach discomfort or stomach pain, or an ulcer or bleeding problem; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; or if you smoke or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with excessive sputum, a cough lasting or recurring for 1 week or more, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or persistent headache.

Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, use it under the supervision of a guardian. Drowsiness may occur after taking it, so take care when driving or operating machinery. If symptoms do not improve after 5 to 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a pharmacist.

Do not take it together with an antitussive-expectorant, another cold medicine, an antipyretic analgesic, a sedative, or an oral medicine containing an antihistamine (oral medicine for rhinitis, motion-sickness medicine, anti-allergy medicine). Consult a pharmacist if you take it together with a diabetes medicine, a gout medicine, an arthritis medicine, an anticoagulant, a steroid, barbiturates, tricyclic antidepressants or alcohol. Do not drink alcohol while taking it.

If rash and reddening of the skin, itching, nausea and vomiting, loss of appetite, constipation, oedema, difficulty passing urine, persistent or severe thirst, dizziness, anxiety, tremor or insomnia occurs, or if, rarely, signs of shock (urticaria, swelling and chest tightness soon after taking it, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), Stevens-Johnson syndrome (mucocutaneous ocular syndrome), toxic epidermal necrolysis (high fever with rash and reddening and severe burn-like blisters), asthma, general lassitude, jaundice or interstitial pneumonia (cough, breathlessness, difficulty breathing, fever) occurs, stop taking this medicine immediately and consult a pharmacist.

summaryTable.Choosing a product: Products with the same generic-name code (130502ALQ) share the same ingredient, strength and dosage form. Check the ingredient and strength rather than the brand name.
summaryTable.Ask the pharmacist: Ask the pharmacist in the store first if any of the cautions above apply to you.
